messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: mcmc::chains's effective sample size
parts:
For some reason this function is slow.  

I am trying to calculate the effective samples size
on the samples of 4 chains (each chain has 50000 iterations)  for the 8-schools model
(actually to see if I have similar results in RStan as a test). 
It takes a couple of minutes to calculate the ESS for a parameter. 

To demonstrate that, I added a fake test as follows, which needs 131138ms to finish
on my computer. 

TEST(McmcChains,effective_sample_size) {
  std::vector<std::string> names;
  std::vector<std::vector<size_t> > dimss;
  stan::mcmc::read_variables("src/test/mcmc/test_csv_files/8schools1.csv", 3,
                             names, dimss);

  stan::mcmc::chains<> c(4, names, dimss);
  add_chain(c, 0, "src/test/mcmc/test_csv_files/8schools1.csv", 3);
  add_chain(c, 1, "src/test/mcmc/test_csv_files/8schools2.csv", 3);
  add_chain(c, 2, "src/test/mcmc/test_csv_files/8schools2.csv", 3);
  add_chain(c, 3, "src/test/mcmc/test_csv_files/8schools2.csv", 3);

  size_t index = 0;
  EXPECT_NEAR(13.08, c.effective_sample_size(index), 0.01) <<
    "the first sample size should be 13.1";
}


In addition, the comments for this function says the formula is from BDA3. 
Can I take a look of this formula?  I might try to find what makes it
slow if I have time. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] mcmc::chains's effective sample size
parts:
I'll send you the pdf for the convergence
formula, which is essentially the same as everyone
else's, but with Andrew's var+ cross-chain variance
estimator in place of each chain's individual estimate.

The easiest way to find the
bottleneck would be by profiling the code.

- Bob
